ladder.teaches: recursion, then memo, then table (climbing stairs)
ladder.why: The last move came from n-1 or n-2; write that as recursion, memoise it, then turn it into a two-variable loop.

ladder.teaches: take or skip on a line (house robber)
ladder.why: Rob house i or skip it: best[i] = max(best[i-1], best[i-2] + nums[i]) is the take-or-skip template.

ladder.teaches: the minimum cost to reach a target (fewest coins)
ladder.why: Climbing stairs with min instead of +: the cheapest way to a stone is the cheaper of its two predecessors plus the jump cost.

ladder.teaches: the minimum cost to reach a target (fewest coins)
ladder.why: Fewest coins: greedy fails, and best[a] = 1 + min(best[a-c]) built from 0 upward, with infinity for unreachable amounts, does not.
Count the ways: the last letter used one or two digits, so add the counts of the two shorter prefixes when each split is valid.

ladder.teaches: DP over prefixes with a dictionary (word break)
ladder.why: ok[i] is true when some dictionary word ends at i and the prefix before it was breakable.

ladder.teaches: Kadane: the best subarray ending here
ladder.why: The best subarray ending here either extends the previous one or restarts; drop a negative running sum.
Define the state by where the subsequence ends (O(n^2)), then speed it up with the tails array and binary search.

notes: 16 rungs for the two plan weeks: the first 8 (core) cover every technique, one per technique except minimum cost, which gets two (frog jump, then coin change). mygate-frog-jump and amd-minimum-coin-change were in no pool and were added with new solutions. Coin change also appears in the knapsack node's technique list (unbounded, fewest coins); the bank has more copies (infosys-minimum-coins-for-target, paytm-minimum-coins-for-target) that knapsack can use. Word break has no OA-style practice rung; the pool's Word Break variants are interview-stage only.
